MRPL Mangalore Refinery — Crude & Vacuum Distillation Unit (CDU/VDU)

Standard Operating Procedure: Crude Blend Optimization & Tower Operations

1. Feed Optimization & Desalting

The Crude Distillation Unit processes crude blends ranging from sweet light crudes (Arab Light, Bonny Light) to heavy sour crudes (Maya, Basrah Heavy). Electrostatic Desalter D-101 maintains salt content below 3.0 PTB and water cut below 0.1% vol to prevent overhead condenser fouling and naphthenic acid corrosion.

2. Column Operating Conditions & Draw Temperatures

3. Furnace F-101 Coil Protection

Crude charge furnace F-101 skin temperatures must not exceed 480°C. Flow meters FT-201 through FT-204 monitor pass balance across the four radiant coils to prevent localized coke deposition.

Standard Operating Manual & Technical Specifications (Document ID: MRPL-SOP-FCCU-2026)

1. Unit Overview & Process Chemistry

The Fluid Catalytic Cracking Unit (FCCU) at Mangalore Refinery processes heavy vacuum gas oil (HVGO) and atmospheric residue blends into high-octane gasoline, light cycle oil (LCO), and LPG. The reaction takes place in a vertical riser reactor with zeolite catalyst particles fluidised by hydrocarbon vapors.

2. Normal Operating Limits & Critical Parameter Matrix

3. Emergency Shutdown & Safety Instrumented System (SIS)

In the event of total electrical failure or loss of combustion air, Emergency Shutdown Valve XV-301 must close within 3.0 seconds to prevent reverse flow of hydrocarbon vapors into the catalyst regenerator. All solenoid valves are powered by 24 VDC redundant uninterruptible power supply (UPS) circuits.

[Table 1]
Header: Parameter | Instrument Tag | Normal Range | Trip Limit / Interlock
Row 1: Parameter: Riser Reactor Outlet Temperature, Instrument Tag: TI-201A/B, Normal Range: 520°C – 540°C, Trip Limit / Interlock: > 555°C (Auto feed cut ESD-501)
Row 2: Parameter: Regenerator Dense Bed Temperature, Instrument Tag: TI-204A-D, Normal Range: 680°C – 715°C, Trip Limit / Interlock: > 740°C (Cyclone metallurgy limit)
Row 3: Parameter: Regenerator Cyclone Differential Pressure, Instrument Tag: DP-401, Normal Range: 12 – 25 kPa, Trip Limit / Interlock: > 35 kPa (Catalyst loss hazard)
Row 4: Parameter: Spent Catalyst Slide Valve Position, Instrument Tag: XV-301, Normal Range: 35% – 65% Open, Trip Limit / Interlock: Fail Close (FC) on low air flow
Row 5: Parameter: Combustion Air Blower Discharge Pressure, Instrument Tag: PT-101, Normal Range: 2.8 – 3.4 bar(g), Trip Limit / Interlock: < 2.2 bar(g) (Trip catalyst circulation)

Standard Operating Manual: High-Pressure Reaction Section & Emergency Procedures

1. Process Description & Reactor Conditions

MRPL operates two identical high-pressure two-stage hydrocrackers (HCU-1 and HCU-2) licensed by Chevron Lummus Global (CLG). The units process heavy vacuum gas oil (HVGO) and coker heavy gas oil (HCGO) over noble/base metal catalysts in a hydrogen-rich atmosphere to produce high-cetane diesel (Cetane Index > 52) and ATF with sulfur levels below 5 ppm.

MRPL operates two identical high-pressure two-stage hydrocrackers (HCU-1 and HCU-2) licensed by Chevron Lummus Global (CLG). The units process heavy vacuum gas oil (HVGO) and coker heavy gas oil (HCGO) over noble/base metal catalysts in a hydrogen-rich atmosphere to produce high-cetane diesel (Cetane Index > 52) and ATF with sulfur levels below 5 ppm.

2. Critical Reaction Parameter Limits

3. Emergency High-Pressure Depressuring (HPE) Protocol

In the event of an uncontrollable temperature runaway (delta-T > 50°C in any catalyst bed) or severe high-pressure hydrogen leak, the operator shall activate the Emergency Depressurization System (EDS). Dual fail-safe valves BDV-701A and BDV-701B will open, depressurizing the reactor loop from 175 bar to 7 bar within 15 minutes as per API-521 standard guidelines.

Row 3: Operating Parameter: Reactor Bed Maximum Delta-T, Normal Range: 25°C – 35°C, Alarm High Limit: > 45°C, Emergency Action / Interlock: Emergency Feed Cutoff; Runaway Reaction Protocol
Row 4: Operating Parameter: Hydrogen Recycle Gas Purity, Normal Range: 88 – 95 mole % H2, Alarm High Limit: < 82 mole % H2, Emergency Action / Interlock: Increase Purge Rate to Fuel Gas; Boost Makeup H2 from HGU
Row 5: Operating Parameter: Recycle Gas Compressor K-601 Suction Drum Level, Normal Range: 30% – 50%, Alarm High Limit: > 70%, Emergency Action / Interlock: Trip Compressor K-601 on High-High Liquid Level to prevent liquid carryover

Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL)

Technical Configuration & Operating Profile (15.0 MMTPA Complex)

1. Corporate & Complex Overview

Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL), a Schedule 'A' Miniratna Central Public Sector Enterprise and a subsidiary of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), operates a state-of-the-art grassroots refinery at Mangalore, Karnataka. The refinery has a nameplate installed capacity of 15.0 Million Metric Tonnes Per Annum (MMTPA) and frequently achieves over 115-120% operational capacity utilization. The complex possesses a high Nelson Complexity Index, enabling it to process heavy, sour, and high-acid crude oils with high distillate recovery.

2. Refinery Configuration by Expansion Phases

3. Unique Refining Distinctions in India

• Dual Hydrocracker Configuration: MRPL is the ONLY refinery in India operating TWO separate Hydrocracker Units (HCU-1 and HCU-2), maximizing the yield of ultra-low sulfur, high-cetane BS-VI high-speed diesel (HSD).
• Deep Residue Upgradation: The Delayed Coker Unit (DCU) converts heavy vacuum residue into high-value distillates and fuel-grade petcoke, eliminating low-value heavy fuel oil production.
• Captive Water & Power Security: Includes a 30 MLD (Million Litres per Day) seawater reverse osmosis desalination plant and captive cogeneration power plant (CPP), ensuring zero dependence on municipal river water during dry seasons.

4. Product Slate

The refinery produces BS-VI Motor Spirit (Petrol), BS-VI High Speed Diesel (HSD), Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF / Jet A-1), Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), Naphtha, Polymer Grade Polypropylene ('Mangpol'), Industrial Bitumen (VG-30, VG-40), Fuel Grade Green Pet Coke, and High Purity Molten/Solid Elemental Sulfur (99.9% purity).

[Table 1]
Header: Expansion Phase | Commissioning Year | Primary Processing Units & Capabilities
Row 1: Expansion Phase: Phase I, Commissioning Year: 1996, Primary Processing Units & Capabilities: CDU-1 & VDU-1 (3.69 MMTPA), Hydrocracker Unit 1 (HCU-1), Hydrogen Generation Unit (HGU-1), Visbreaker Unit (VBU), Bitumen Blowing Unit (BBU), Sulfur Recovery Unit (SRU-1).
Row 2: Expansion Phase: Phase II, Commissioning Year: 1999–2000, Primary Processing Units & Capabilities: CDU-2 & VDU-2 (5.9 MMTPA expansion), Continuous Catalytic Regeneration Platformer (CCR-1 & CCR-2) for high-octane MS, Additional SRU trains, Diesel Hydro Desulfurization (DHDS).
Row 3: Expansion Phase: Phase III, Commissioning Year: 2012–2014, Primary Processing Units & Capabilities: CDU-3 & VDU-3 (3.0 MMTPA), Hydrocracker Unit 2 (HCU-2), Petrochemical Fluidized Catalytic Cracking Unit (PFCCU, 2.2 MMTPA), Delayed Coker Unit (DCU, 3.0 MMTPA), Polypropylene Plant (PPU, 440 KTPA, 'Mangpol'), Diesel Hydrotreater (DHDT).

Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL)

Technical Configuration & Operating Profile (15.0 MMTPA Complex)

1. Corporate & Complex Overview

Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL), a Schedule 'A' Miniratna Central Public Sector Enterprise and a subsidiary of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), operates a state-of-the-art grassroots refinery at Mangalore, Karnataka. The refinery has a nameplate installed capacity of 15.0 Million Metric Tonnes Per Annum (MMTPA) and frequently achieves over 115-120% operational capacity utilization. The complex possesses a high Nelson Complexity Index, enabling it to process heavy, sour, and high-acid crude oils with high distillate recovery.

2. Refinery Configuration by Expansion Phases

3. Unique Refining Distinctions in India

• Dual Hydrocracker Configuration: MRPL is the ONLY refinery in India operating TWO separate Hydrocracker Units (HCU-1 and HCU-2), maximizing the yield of ultra-low sulfur, high-cetane BS-VI high-speed diesel (HSD).
• Deep Residue Upgradation: The Delayed Coker Unit (DCU) converts heavy vacuum residue into high-value distillates and fuel-grade petcoke, eliminating low-value heavy fuel oil production.
• Captive Water & Power Security: Includes a 30 MLD (Million Litres per Day) seawater reverse osmosis desalination plant and captive cogeneration power plant (CPP), ensuring zero dependence on municipal river water during dry seasons.

4. Product Slate

The refinery produces BS-VI Motor Spirit (Petrol), BS-VI High Speed Diesel (HSD), Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF / Jet A-1), Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), Naphtha, Polymer Grade Polypropylene ('Mangpol'), Industrial Bitumen (VG-30, VG-40), Fuel Grade Green Pet Coke, and High Purity Molten/Solid Elemental Sulfur (99.9% purity).

Row 2: Expansion Phase: Phase II, Commissioning Year: 1999–2000, Primary Processing Units & Capabilities: CDU-2 & VDU-2 (5.9 MMTPA expansion), Continuous Catalytic Regeneration Platformer (CCR-1 & CCR-2) for high-octane MS, Additional SRU trains, Diesel Hydro Desulfurization (DHDS).
Row 3: Expansion Phase: Phase III, Commissioning Year: 2012–2014, Primary Processing Units & Capabilities: CDU-3 & VDU-3 (3.0 MMTPA), Hydrocracker Unit 2 (HCU-2), Petrochemical Fluidized Catalytic Cracking Unit (PFCCU, 2.2 MMTPA), Delayed Coker Unit (DCU, 3.0 MMTPA), Polypropylene Plant (PPU, 440 KTPA, 'Mangpol'), Diesel Hydrotreater (DHDT).

MRPL Mangalore Refinery — Single Point Mooring (SPM) Operations

Standard Operating Procedure: Offshore VLCC Crude Tanker Unloading (SOP-SPM-2026-02)

1. SPM Facility Description

MRPL operates a Single Point Mooring (SPM) terminal located approximately 16.5 kilometers offshore New Mangalore Port at a water depth of 32 meters. The terminal can handle Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) up to 300,000 DWT. Crude oil is pumped from the tanker through two 24-inch floating hoses, the SPM swivel, a pipeline end manifold (PLEM), and a 48-inch subsea pipeline to the onshore coastal crude oil terminal (CCOT) at Kasaba and onward to the refinery.

2. Discharge Operations & Pressure Surge Limits

Oil Industry Safety Directorate — OISD Standard 156

Fire Protection & Toxic Gas Detection Facilities for Petroleum Refineries

1. Scope and Mandatory Provisions

This standard lays down minimum requirements for fixed fire protection, hydrocarbon gas detection, and toxic gas monitoring (H2S and SO2) systems in hydrocarbon processing plants, tank farms, and LPG storage spheres.

2. Gas Detector Allocation & Alarm Thresholds

[Table 1]
Header: Gas Hazard | Detector Type | Alarm 1 (Low Alert) | Alarm 2 (High / Auto Deluge)
Row 1: Gas Hazard: Flammable Hydrocarbon Vapor, Detector Type: Catalytic / IR Open Path, Alarm 1 (Low Alert): 20% LEL (Audible beacon), Alarm 2 (High / Auto Deluge): 60% LEL (Trip fuel gas & start water spray)
Row 2: Gas Hazard: Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S), Detector Type: Electrochemical Sensor, Alarm 1 (Low Alert): 10 ppm (Mandatory breathing gear), Alarm 2 (High / Auto Deluge): 20 ppm (Evacuate unit & ESD isolation)
Row 3: Gas Hazard: Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), Detector Type: Optical / Electrochemical, Alarm 1 (Low Alert): 2 ppm (Warning alert), Alarm 2 (High / Auto Deluge): 5 ppm (SRU unit shutdown)

Standard Operating Procedure: Hydrocarbon Freeing, Blinding, and Vessel Entry (SOP-TA-2026-01)

Prior to breaking flanges or unheading columns, all battery limit connections must be isolated with spectacle blinds or spade plates as per the Master Blind List. Blind installation must be verified by two independent engineers.

2. Confined Space Vessel Entry Criteria

[Table 1]
Header: Atmospheric Parameter | Permissible Safe Entry Limit | Testing Frequency
Row 1: Atmospheric Parameter: Oxygen (O2) Concentration, Permissible Safe Entry Limit: 19.5% to 23.5% vol, Testing Frequency: Continuous during entry
Row 2: Atmospheric Parameter: Combustible Hydrocarbon Gas, Permissible Safe Entry Limit: < 1.0% LEL (strictly 0.0% preferred), Testing Frequency: Every 2 hours or shift handover
Row 3: Atmospheric Parameter: Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S), Permissible Safe Entry Limit: < 5.0 ppm, Testing Frequency: Continuous portable gas monitor
Row 4: Atmospheric Parameter: Carbon Monoxide (CO), Permissible Safe Entry Limit: < 25.0 ppm, Testing Frequency: Before every permit re-validation
